newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AMG gets Anglo deal on JCI stake.
newsitem.headline: AMG gets Anglo deal on JCI stake.

text.p: The African Mining Group and Anglo American Corp have sealed a historic deal in which AGM bought the remainder of Anglo's holding in mining house JCI Ltd, the Sunday Times newspaper reported.

AMG -- which groups Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd, African Renaissance Holdings and Khotso Investments among others -- agreed last November to buy a 34.9 percent stake in JCI from Anglo for 2.88 billion rand ($642 million) or 54.40 rand per share.
The deal, which gives black business a significant stake in the South African mining industry for the first time, was sealed on Friday, the Sunday Times said.
It sets the scene for a bid by the consortium to buy Anglo's remaining 12.7 percent stake in the mining house, giving it unfettered control of JCI.
AMG has been given the right of first refusal to the stake for a period of five years, the Sunday Times said.
The JCI board will be reconstituted in March and Mzi Khumalo of Capital Alliance appointed as chairman, the paper added.
"We've complied with all of Anglo's conditions and the deal is done," Khumalo told the Sunday Times.
The deal was struck a full week ahead of the February 28 deadline.
Khumalo told the Sunday Times that Saflife, the listed life assurance company which controls 25.9 percent of Capital Alliance, would be the vehicle through which the deal is done.

The paper said Saflife would raise 1.4 billion rand of the money while other institutions -- believed to be Investec, SBC Warburg and Standard Corporate Merchant Bank -- are underwriting the remaining amount.
Further details of the transaction are expected on Monday.

The deal, the second largest empowerment deal ever following the National Empowerment Consortium's acquisition of a 35 percent stake in Johnnic for three billion rand, heralds the entry of black buisness to the mining indsutry, the paper said.
JCI is South Africa's sixth-largest mining house and controls three gold mines, two of them considered among the most profitable in the country.

The Sunday Times said the acquisition effectively increased the market capitalisation of black-controlled or managed companies on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) to about 30 billion rand, based on Friday's trading prices -- slightly over three percent of the JSE's total capitalisation.
And taking into account Johnnic's interests in other listed entities, the paper said, this figure is close to 11 percent of the JSE's market capitalisation.
